edition: ETA Associate CET Study Guide Sixth Edition (personal scanned copy)
sourcePagination: Printed p maps to PDF page p+9 for numbered body
copyrightNote: Audit notes only; do not embed copyrighted excerpts in this manifest
reviewLevel: printed-page topical alignment, NOT exhaustive sentence-by-sentence technical verification

readings.currentLessonTitle: Lockout, stored energy and verification
readings.sourceEvidence: Safety, electric shock, bench equipment and vintage devices are discussed; the old first-aid and energized-work recommendations must not substitute for modern professional guidance.
readings.guidedRetrievalTask: After studying Alfred safety protocols, identify two unsafe assumptions in vintage bench or first-aid discussions. Apply current qualified procedures, not book-era examples.

readings.currentLessonTitle: SI prefixes: communicating scale without losing units
readings.sourceEvidence: The assigned pages cover math, engineering prefixes and electrical formulas; the opening page contains introduction as well as examples.
readings.guidedRetrievalTask: Convert three quantities between SI prefixes, write each result with its unit and check one power/Ohm-law relationship.

readings.currentLessonTitle: Comparing P = VI, I²R and V²/R
readings.sourceEvidence: Printed page 27 explicitly discusses power changes with resistance and current and DC circuit relationships.
readings.guidedRetrievalTask: From P = I²R and P = V²/R, explain what is held constant before predicting how power changes.

readings.currentLessonTitle: Loaded divider: why a measurement or circuit changes Vout
readings.sourceEvidence: Printed pages 27–31 present DC series/parallel resistor networks and a classic tube B+ voltage divider; a modern loaded-divider model needs additional Alfred instruction.
readings.guidedRetrievalTask: Compute the book series/parallel reduction, then use Alfred to include the loading resistance of a measured divider.

readings.currentLessonTitle: Schematic, wiring and layout: practice moving between views
readings.sourceEvidence: Printed pages 161–162 concern schematic drawings, service information and symbolic circuit tracing.
readings.guidedRetrievalTask: Follow an input-to-output path using both a schematic and block diagram; identify where you would measure.

readings.currentLessonTitle: Capacitive and inductive reactance
readings.sourceEvidence: Printed pages 19–22 contain capacitor calculations, time constants and reactive circuit reasoning, not a comprehensive modern capacitor construction/polarity survey.
readings.guidedRetrievalTask: Solve the book capacitor/reactance exercise. Revisit Alfred separately for polarized-device safety and component selection.

readings.currentLessonTitle: From impedance to an equivalent circuit
readings.sourceEvidence: Printed pages 45–49 discuss AC behavior, reactance and series/parallel circuit relationships. Official errata apply to some pages.
readings.guidedRetrievalTask: Identify the resistive and reactive contributions to impedance and predict how frequency alters current.

readings.currentLessonTitle: Motor and generator: opposite energy directions
readings.sourceEvidence: Chapter 7 printed pages 53–57 address generator, alternator and motor machines. This is not a first-use primer on transformer primary/secondary operation.
readings.guidedRetrievalTask: Compare a motor and a generator; explain how field and conductor motion affect the direction of energy conversion.

readings.currentLessonTitle: Zener operation in reverse breakdown
readings.sourceEvidence: Printed pages 72–73 and 75–76 cover semiconductor junctions and device families, with a brief treatment of specialty diodes. They cannot alone establish full Zener and SCR competence.
readings.guidedRetrievalTask: Identify the role of the junction and distinguish a regulator diode from a switching/controlled device; use Alfred for datasheet limits.

readings.currentLessonTitle: Linear regulators and headroom
readings.sourceEvidence: Printed pages 85–89 cover transformer and rectifier supply blocks, filtering, ripple and regulation.
readings.guidedRetrievalTask: Sketch rectifier → filter → regulator and identify how a poor capacitor or regulator changes output ripple.

readings.currentLessonTitle: Measuring gain without fooling yourself
readings.sourceEvidence: The selected pages discuss amplifier classes, push-pull operation and decibel power ratios; they are not a direct step-by-step treatment of modern op-amp inverting gain.
readings.guidedRetrievalTask: Compare amplifier class behavior and solve the book dB gain example; then use Alfred for the inverting op-amp formula.

readings.currentLessonTitle: Place value: one quantity, different bases
readings.sourceEvidence: Printed pages 132–140 introduce base conversions, logic gates, binary operations and sequential logic. This broad selection spans several lessons.
readings.guidedRetrievalTask: Convert a number in binary/octal/hex, then explain one truth table and one sequential behavior without looking.

readings.currentLessonTitle: CPU blocks and control flow
readings.sourceEvidence: Printed pages 149–150 describe computer architecture, processor operations, instructions and memory addressing.
readings.guidedRetrievalTask: Trace a basic instruction fetch/decode/execute sequence and identify what changes in memory or registers.

readings.currentLessonTitle: Copper pair, coaxial and optical signal paths
readings.sourceEvidence: The inherited pp.108–109 emphasize antennas and the ionosphere; pp.109–110 directly introduce coax cable charts, shields, center conductors and characteristic signal-path properties. The corrected selection is still only partial cabling coverage.
readings.guidedRetrievalTask: Using pp.109–110, explain the center conductor, dielectric and shield. Use Alfred and current cable standards for crimp, bonding and fiber practice.

readings.currentLessonTitle: Photocells, photodiodes and photovoltaic sources
readings.sourceEvidence: Printed page 77 discusses light-responsive semiconductor devices including phototransistors. This does not fully cover modern LCD/OLED displays or optical sensors.
readings.guidedRetrievalTask: Distinguish photodiode, phototransistor and photovoltaic functions; separately review modern displays in Alfred.

readings.currentLessonTitle: Receiver blocks: antenna to intelligible output
readings.sourceEvidence: Printed pages 104–107 focus on radio receiver sections: antenna/RF amplification, local oscillator/mixer, IF, detection and AGC. They better match the receiver-block lesson than the introductory electromagnetic-propagation page.
readings.guidedRetrievalTask: Trace a received radio signal through antenna, RF stage, local oscillator/mixer, IF stage, detection and AGC.

readings.currentLessonTitle: Modulation: how a message rides on a carrier
readings.sourceEvidence: Printed pages 113–114 describe modulation mechanisms and communication system examples.
readings.guidedRetrievalTask: Explain which carrier characteristic changes for AM versus FM and identify the information signal.

readings.currentLessonTitle: Simplex, duplex and repeaters
readings.sourceEvidence: Printed pages 120–121 explain historic telephone systems and simplex/duplex terms. Modern packet, VoIP, cellular and fiber topics go beyond this limited old-textbook excerpt.
readings.guidedRetrievalTask: Define simplex, half-duplex and full-duplex. Contrast analog voice switching with packet-network transport taught in Alfred.

readings.currentLessonTitle: Handoffs prevent repeat mistakes
readings.sourceEvidence: Printed pages 182–184 discuss record keeping, technician handoffs and time or service documentation.
readings.guidedRetrievalTask: Draft a service handoff with observed symptoms, measurements, work completed and next action.

readings.currentLessonTitle: Traceable reports tie evidence to work
readings.sourceEvidence: Printed pages 188–190 introduce technical writing and structured reports.
readings.guidedRetrievalTask: Prepare a concise troubleshooting report with method, evidence, conclusion and remaining uncertainty.
